fact_sheet.business_description: The Company designs and manufactures PC and server processors and owns an extensive semiconductor fabrication base [D01]. It faces strategic challenges in restoring engineering execution and competing against fabless rivals and customers designing their own chips [D01].
segments_and_separable_assets: Core processor design and manufacturing operations (Q3 2020 revenue $18.333bn) [D03]
Memory/storage business (sale announced for $9bn, subject to conditions) [D03]
economics_vs_peers: The Company's Q3 2020 gross margin was 53.1% (GAAP) compared to 58.9% in the prior year [D02, D06].
Competitors include AMD (9.4% operating margin FY2019), Nvidia (26.1% operating margin FY2020), and Texas Instruments (39.8% operating margin FY2019) [D06].
The Company faces lower returns on fabrication investment compared to fabless peers [D01, D06].
capital_structure: Cash and short-term investments of $18.253bn as of 2020-09-26 [D04].
Net debt of $18.31bn (broader measure) as of 2020-09-26 [D04].
management_board_governance: CEO: Bob Swan; Chair: Omar Ishrak [D07].
Prior activist history: not in pack.
shareholder_base_and_liquidity: Top holders/index ownership: not in pack.

Loss of product share to fabless competitors [D01, D05].
High capex requirements depressing free cash flow [D01, D05].
Customers designing their own chips [D01, D05].

event_identified.evidence: The company suffers from a significant manufacturing/process gap against fabless peers and internal product slippage, presenting a classic activist opportunity for operational refocusing or structural separation [D01, D06].

edge.evidence: Third Point brings a track record of mega-cap constructivism to address the company's valuation discount and operational issues, leveraging our experience in corporate governance to drive change [D05, D08].

governance_route_or_process.evidence: As a $200bn market cap company, it is widely held, providing a sufficient institutional base to pressure a board that has presided over significant loss of technological leadership [D04, D01].

downside_floor.evidence: The business is trading at a depressed TTM P/E of 9.70x with a strong 10.04% FCF yield, providing a valuation floor that limits downside even during the current turnaround [D04].

size_and_liquidity.evidence: With 4,098 million shares outstanding and high trading liquidity, Third Point can establish a significant position within our target sizing range [D04, D08].

management_credibility.evidence: The current management has overseen a documented decline in process leadership and margin compression, necessitating either an immediate shift in strategic direction or leadership replacement [D01, D02, D07].

Strategic separation of the manufacturing assets or a radical pivot in operational focus will unlock this value, correcting the margin gap against more efficient peers [D01, D06].

drivers.driver: The Company is a deeply undervalued technology incumbent suffering from a broken, inefficient integrated manufacturing model that masks the intrinsic value of its core design business.
Trading at 9.7x TTM P/E with a 10.04% FCF yield, the stock provides a hard valuation floor and an asymmetric risk/reward skew of nearly 3:1.
Structural separation of manufacturing assets or a radical strategic pivot is required to close the margin gap against more efficient fabless peers like Nvidia and TI.
We are initiating a public campaign to press the board to evaluate structural alternatives and restore engineering execution, leveraging our experience in mega-cap constructivism.

final.memo:
Intel is a world-class engineering institution currently suffering from a severe crisis of leadership and operational focus. While the Company remains a titan of the semiconductor industry, it has lost its manufacturing edge and faces a widening margin gap compared to fabless peers who have successfully outsourced production [D01, D06]. We believe the Company is profoundly mispriced, as the market values this business at a depressed 9.7x TTM P/E, ignoring the intrinsic value of its core design operations and a healthy 10.04% FCF yield [D04].

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis, which models post-restructuring FCF of $22bn at a 13x peer-adjusted multiple, implies a valuation of $78 per share [D03, D04, D06]. This represents a significant discount to its intrinsic potential, providing us with an asymmetric 58% upside against a hard floor supported by current cash flow [D04].

The market has the Company wrong because it treats an operational failure as a permanent decline in the business franchise. We believe this is an inflection point where the board must acknowledge that the integrated model—once a source of strength—is now a drag on value [D01, D02, D06]. Our engagement plan is direct: we are demanding that CEO Bob Swan and Chair Omar Ishrak evaluate structural alternatives, including the separation of design and manufacturing, and pivot capital allocation back toward core R&D [D06, D07].

We are committed to using our platform as shareholders to drive this change, and we are prepared to escalate our public pressure if management proves unwilling to address these systemic issues [D08]. Our thesis rests on the belief that a focused, leaner, and more strategically aligned Intel will regain its leadership status and close the margin gap with fabless competitors [D01, D06]. We are initiating a 5% position in the common shares, hedged with SOX index puts to manage sector-wide volatility, and we look forward to immediate engagement with the board [D08].
